'''Kurt Martin Mislow''' (June 5, 1923 – October 5, 2017) was a German-born American [[organic chemistry|organic chemist]] who specialized in [[stereochemistry]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Siegel | first1=J. S. | title=Kurt M. Mislow (1923-2017) | journal=Angewandte Chemie (International ed. In English) | date=2018 | volume=57 | issue=18 | page=4835 | doi=10.1002/anie.201800131 | pmid=29573525 | bibcode=2018ACIE...57.4835S }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Born in Berlin on June 5, 1923, Mislow had moved to London by 1938, after some time in Milan. With the help of his uncle [[Alfred Eisenstaedt]], Mislow's family left London for New York City in 1940. Mislow earned a bachelor's degree in chemistry from [[Tulane University]] in 1944, and received a doctorate from the [[California Institute of Technology]], where he was supervised by [[Linus Pauling]].<ref name="pobit" /> His thesis was entitled: I. The Synthesis of Potential Antimaterials. Some 2-Substituted 8-(3-Diethylaminopropylaminol)-Quinolines. II. Isomorphism in Relation to Serological Specificity. III. A Study of the [[Hammick reaction|Hammick Reaction]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2004 |title=I. The Synthesis of Potential Antimaterials. Some 2-Substituted 8-(3-Diethylaminopropylaminol)-Quinolines. II. Isomorphism in Relation to Serological Specificity. III. A Study of the Hammick Reaction |url=https://thesis.library.caltech.edu/2579/ |website=Caltech Coda}}</ref> 

== Career and research ==
Mislow first taught at [[New York University]], then moved to [[Princeton University]] in 1964. While at Princeton, Mislow served as [[Hugh Stott Taylor|Hugh Stott Taylor Professor of Chemistry]] and led the chemistry department from 1968 to 1974. He became a professor emeritus in 1988.<ref name="pobit">{{cite news|title=Kurt Mislow, pioneer in stereochemistry, dies at 94|url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2017/10/27/kurt-mislow-pioneer-stereochemistry-dies-94|accessdate=October 29, 2017|publisher=Princeton University|date=October 27, 2017}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Over the course of his career, Mislow was named a Guggenheim fellow twice, in 1956 and 1974. Between 1959 and 1963, Mislow was granted the [[Sloan Research Fellowship]]. He became a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1972, followed by fellowships in the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], granted in 1974, and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], bestowed in 1980. In 1999, Mislow was named a foreign member of the [[Accademia dei Lincei]]. The [[American Chemical Society]] honored Mislow with several awards, among them the [[James Flack Norris Award for Outstanding Achievement in the Teaching of Chemistry|James Flack Norris Award]] in Physical Organic Chemistry (1975), the [[William H. Nichols Medal Award]] (1987), and the [[Arthur C. Cope Scholar Award]] (1995).<ref name="pobit"/>

== Personal life ==
Mislow died at the age of 94 years on Oct. 5, 2017. He was survived by his wife, son, and two grandsons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wang |first=Linda |date=20 November 2017 |title=Obituary: Kurt Mislow |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/95/i46/Kurt-Mislow.html |website=Chemical & Engineering News}}</ref>
